body: @aj7 It would be very helpful if you can create a minimal reproduction scenario (data + API calls / curl commands).

@danielmitterdorfer Sure, I have put the info in the [gist](https://gist.github.com/aj7/307b4577dbe52601c5e7b940d81450cd)

Hope this is fine?

I have nothing to add to this ticket other than to +1 @aj7 on this issue.  We too have seen this error with either high vertex count polygons or polygons with very high precision.  Sometime the workaround is to simplify the geometry with something like PostGIS but often that can compromise the data.  
And, for what it's worth, it's not too hard to generate polygons like this (imagine a highly precise polygon representing country borders).
We would love for this to be fixed, as we've run into this on more then one occasion.

We also faced with this issue
Simple example cause
"java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: -1
	at org.elasticsearch.common.geo.builders.PolygonBuilder.assign(PolygonBuilder.java:483)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.geo.builders.PolygonBuilder.compose(PolygonBuilder.java:455)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.geo.builders.PolygonBuilder.coordinates(PolygonBuilder.java:221)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.geo.builders.PolygonBuilder.buildGeometry(PolygonBuilder.java:251)
	at org.elasticsearch.common.geo.builders.PolygonBuilder.build(PolygonBuilder.java:226)
	at 


{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[-10,10.0000000000002],[-5,-5],[10,5],[-10,10.0000000000002]],[[-10,10],[0,5],[0,0],[-10,10]]]}

This seems to be because of an error in the geometry you're trying to index, although it would certainly be helpful if there was a more descriptive error message given. The attached zip file, for instance, contains self-intersections so I think it's right to reject it.

Here is a shorter reproduction:

```
$ curl -XDELETE "http://localhost:9200/speedlimit"
{"acknowledged":true}
$ curl -XPUT "http://localhost:9200/speedlimit" -H'Content-type: application/json' -d '{"mappings":{"speedlimit":{"properties":{"geometry":{"type":"geo_shape","tree":"quadtree","precision":"100m"}}}}}'
{"acknowledged":true,"shards_acknowledged":true,"index":"speedlimit"}
$ curl -XPOST "http://localhost:9200/speedlimit/speedlimit" -H'Content-type: application/json' -d '{"geometry":{"coordinates":[[[[4,3],[3,2],[3,3],[4,3]],[[4,2],[3,1],[4,1],[4,2]]]],"type":"MultiPolygon"}}'
{"error":{"root_cause":[{"type":"mapper_parsing_exception","reason":"failed to parse [geometry]"}],"type":"mapper_parsing_exception","reason":"failed to parse [geometry]","caused_by":{"type":"array_index_out_of_bounds_exception","reason":"-1"}},"status":400}
```

In this case the given geometry contains two triangles, the first of which is clockwise and the second is anticlockwise, indicating that one is an enclave (hole) within the other. However the triangles do not touch.

@rkuchvarskyy the example you give also is not a valid geometry because the "hole" is not completely within the outer polygon. It's too small to see the error, but if I exaggerate the problem a bit your shape looks like this:
@DaveCTurner I understood this but I expect some validation exception but not java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

issue.title: Handle case where the hole vertex is south of the containing polygon(s)

labels.name: :Analytics/Geo
labels.description: Indexing, search aggregations of geo points and shapes

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Normally the hole is assigned to the component of the first edge to the south
of one of its vertices, but if the chosen hole vertex is south of everything
then the binary search returns -1 yielding an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
Instead, assign the vertex to the component of the first edge to its north.
Subsequent validation catches the fact that the hole is outside its component.

Fixes #25933
